papers.title_in_file: Implementing Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (qGAN) and QCBM in Finance
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods and results, conclusion (whole text via plain pdftotext)
papers.what_it_is: A short paper that runs a qGAN and a QCBM on Binance crypto-currency price data in a Qiskit simulator.

assertions.value: The authors state that they implemented the qGAN and the QCBM on real Binance data using the IBM Qiskit simulator.
quotes: A study of implementations of qGAN and QCBM were done using real life Binance data on Qiskit simulator from IBM.
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion states the setup: a simulator run.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no run on quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that data samples below the 5% percentile and above the 95% percentile were discarded to reduce the number of qubits required.
quotes: Data samples smaller than 5% percentile and bigger than 95% percentile were discarded to reduce the number of qubits required for a reasonable representation of the distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III.A states the data preparation step.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the qGAN produced expected results in far fewer iterations than a classical GAN would take.
quotes: The qGAN produced expected results in far less iterations than it would take a classical GAN.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim in the conclusion. The quoted text gives no iteration counts for either model.
assertions.reader_inference: Run on a simulator with no stated classical baseline in the quoted text.

assertions.value: The authors report that Cobyla was marginally better than SPSA as an optimizer for the QCBM, yet the Cobyla distribution had wider gaps to the real data.
quotes: Cobyla was found to be marginally better than SPSA.
Comparison of the real data with Cobyla had wider gaps with the real fdata even though Cobyla, as an optimizer, gave better results.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical comparison on one data set; the paper reads the visual fit from figures.

papers.title_in_file: On the relation between trainability and dequantization of variational quantum learning models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, definitions, Proposition 1, Theorem 3, Corollaries, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: An ICLR 2025 theory paper that defines trainability and dequantization and proves variational QML models can be both trainable and non-dequantizable.

assertions.value: The paper proves that variational QML models exist that are gradient-based trainable and non-dequantizable.
quotes: there do exist variational QML models which are trainable and non-dequantizable.
Corollary 2. There exist deep-layered circuits, like Deep HEA, which are trainable and nondequantizable.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3 and Corollary 4; summarized in Section 6.
assertions.reader_inference: The existence result rests on a constructed model, not a natural one (see the limit assertion).

assertions.value: The paper proves that QML models exist that have barren plateaus under the uniform distribution of parameters and are still trainable on classically intractable tasks.
quotes: There exist QML models which have BPs under the uniform distribution of parameters and are trainable for learning tasks that are classically intractable under standard cryptographic assumptions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposition 1.

assertions.value: The paper defines a learning model as trainable if the empirical risk of the hypothesis from the learning algorithm is close to the optimal one within the class, with high probability, for each task of interest.
quotes: a learning model (F, A) is trainable if the following holds for each task: the empirical risk of the hypothesis produced by the learning algorithm is close to the optimal one within the class
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that their constructed models could be qualified as contrived, that the solution is planted in the hypothesis family, and that they treated supervised learning only.
quotes: the models we have designed could be qualified as contrived
The way in which we ensured that our QML models would solve the problem was by planting the solution in the architecture of the hypothesis family itself.
In this work we discussed exclusively supervised learning scenarios
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5 states these limits in the authors' own words.

papers.title_in_file: An introduction to variational quantum algorithms for combinatorial optimization problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, QAOA literature section and conclusion; definitions skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial on variational quantum algorithms with a focus on QAOA and a survey of the QAOA literature.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper is a tutorial giving a mathematical description of variational quantum algorithms for readers with no prior knowledge of quantum physics.
quotes: In this tutorial, we provide a mathematical description of the class of Variational Quantum Algorithms, assuming no previous knowledge of quantum physics from the readers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that this research seems to indicate that there is currently no scientific evidence that QAOA will soon beat classical heuristics.
quotes: This research seems to indicate that there is currently no scientific evidence that QAOA will soon beat classical heuristics.
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey judgment drawn from other works, not a result of this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that current numerical results are hard to assess because they are run on small instances that classical algorithms can solve to optimal or near-optimal quality.
quotes: the current numerical results are hard to assess because they are run on small instances for which optimal or near-optimal solutions can be obtained easily with classical algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey judgment about the literature.

assertions.value: The authors report, citing another work, that Goemans-Williamson outperforms QAOA on several MAX-CUT instances for any fixed depth p.
quotes: they show that Goemans-Williamson outperforms QAOA for several instances of the MAX-CUT problem for any fixed depth p.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to reference [4], not shown in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum computer based Feature Selection in Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results sections, extension to 27 features, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A study that casts feature selection as a QUBO and solves it classically and with QAOA on simulators and IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that, because of persisting error rates, classical stochastic optimization methods are still superior to the quantum approach, and that the classical and meta-heuristical methods are not outperformed at current qubit numbers.
quotes: Due to persisting error rates, the classical stochastic optimization methods are still superior.
With the number of qubits available at the moment, the classical and meta-heuristical methods are not outperformed by quantum computing.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report approximation ratios above 0.80 on real IBM hardware, well above the random sampling result, for the larger problem with 27 features.
quotes: on real hardware we obtained approximation ratios above 0.80; well above the random sampling result.
In an extension to a larger data set with 27 features
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study and one problem.

assertions.value: The authors state that whether the QUBO method outperforms other feature selection methods depends on the data set, in small-sized problem setups.
quotes: According to the results of our study, whether the QUBO method outperforms other feature selection methods depends on the data set.
We compare the different results in small-sized problem setups.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scaling of the classical and quantum approaches, and the qubit number at which a quantum advantage may appear, is an open question left to future work.
quotes: An open question that will be addressed in future work is the scaling of both approaches, i.e. if and for which number of qubits there may be a quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion states the limit of the study.

papers.title_in_file: Comparing Quantum Annealing and Spiking Neuromorphic Computing for Sampling Binary Sparse Coding QUBO Problems
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark that samples sparse-coding QUBOs on a D-Wave annealer, on Intel Loihi 2, and with simulated annealing and CPLEX.

assertions.value: The authors report that iterated reverse quantum annealing performs similarly to simulated annealing, but simulated annealing always sampled the optimal solution while quantum annealing did not.
quotes: Iterated reverse quantum annealing performs similarly to simulated annealing, although simulated annealing is always able to sample the optimal solution whereas quantum annealing was not always able to.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on the QUBO sizes studied.

assertions.value: The authors report that Loihi 2 samples are on average more sparse than the other methods, and that Loihi 2 outperforms a standard linear-schedule D-Wave anneal.
quotes: The Loihi 2 solutions that are sampled are on average more sparse than the solutions from any of the other methods.
Loihi 2 outperforms a D-Wave quantum annealer standard linear-schedule anneal
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the solutions are benchmarked against simulated annealing and that optimal solutions are computed with CPLEX.
quotes: The solutions are benchmarked against simulated annealing, a classical heuristic, and the optimal solutions are computed using CPLEX.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that coefficient precision limits on current D-Wave devices are almost certainly the most important reason the annealing runs did not reach the global minimum, but they offer this as a possible reason, not a tested one.
quotes: Amongst others, the following reasons might have impeded the forward annealing and reverse annealing sampling from reaching the global minimum in our experiments.
The first, and almost certainly the most important, is the coefficient precision limits that can be programmed on current D-Wave devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author hypothesis in the Discussion; no test is quoted.

papers.title_in_file: Gradient Estimation with Constant Scaling for Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, experiments, results, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A Quantinuum paper that applies multivariate SPSA inside backpropagation (SPSB) to estimate PQC gradients at constant circuit cost.

assertions.value: The authors state that SPSB gradients of PQC layers need an overhead of two evaluations per circuit per forward pass, independent of the number of circuit parameters, compared with the linear scaling of the parameter shift rule.
quotes: The gradients of PQC layers can be calculated with an overhead of two evaluations per circuit per forward-pass independent of the number of circuit parameters, compared to the linear scaling of the parameter shift rule.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe their own method; the paper gives no formal proof in the quoted text.

assertions.value: The authors report that as the number of qubits increases their method converges significantly faster than the parameter shift rule, to comparable accuracy, even at the optimal learning rate for each.
quotes: We find that, as the number of qubits increases, our method converges significantly faster than the parameter shift rule and to a comparable accuracy, even when considering the optimal learning rate for each method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on small test models.

assertions.value: The authors report that for very low batch sizes SPSB does not always find the global minimum, while parameter-shift gradients are unaffected by batch size.
quotes: we find that for very low batch sizes the global minimum is not always found, while the performance using parameter-shift gradients is unaffected by the batch size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5 states this limit of the method.

assertions.value: The authors state that one test task is binary classification on 100 randomly initialised datapoints.
quotes: We generate 100 datapoints for a binary classification task
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4.1 states the test setup.

papers.title_in_file: Tensor Network Based Efficient Quantum Data Loading of Images
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method and results text, conclusion (two-column layout read from plain extraction)
papers.what_it_is: An IonQ paper that loads images as approximate amplitude encodings using matrix-product-state circuits, with a demonstration on 8 qubits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the gates and qubits of the method scale logarithmically in the number of pixels for a desired accuracy.
quotes: The numbers of gates and qubits in our method scale logarithmically in the number of pixels given a desired accuracy, which make it suitable for near term quantum computers.
We have shown through numerical testing that the technique has favorable scaling properties in terms of the circuit depths required to reach desired fidelities.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own numerical testing.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental demonstration on 8 qubits of a trapped ion quantum computer for road-scene images, and call it the first large instance of full amplitude encoding of an image.
quotes: we experimentally demonstrate our technique on 8 qubits of a trapped ion quantum computer for complex images of road scenes, making this the first large instance of full amplitude encoding of an image in a quantum state.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single demonstration; the first-of-its-kind wording is the authors' claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method creates quantum states that approximately encode images as amplitudes.
quotes: Here we present a novel method for creating quantum states that approximately encode images as amplitudes, based on recently proposed techniques that convert matrix product states to quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the scope: approximate, not exact, encoding.

papers.what_it_is: An Oxford paper that proposes a hybrid quantum-classical contrastive learning architecture and tests it on CIFAR-10 in simulation and on ibmq paris.

assertions.value: The authors report a numerical advantage for learning visual representations with small-scale quantum neural networks over equivalently structured classical networks, even with only 100 shots.
quotes: we observe a numerical advantage for the learning of visual representations using small-scale quantum neural networks over equivalently structured classical networks, even when the quantum circuits are sampled with only 100 shots.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from small simulated models on one data set.
assertions.reader_inference: Simulator result; the paper itself notes how to compare quantum and classical networks fairly is an open question.

assertions.value: The authors report that on ibmq paris, on 900 test images, the classical and quantum models reached 47.27% and 47.00% accuracy respectively.
quotes: classifying 900 images randomly sampled from the test set
Overall, the classical and quantum models achieve an accuracy of 47.27% and 47.00% respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware experiment with a frozen pretrained model.

assertions.value: The authors state that experimental quantum advantage would need a QNN wider than 60 qubits, and that the scheme was only demonstrated at small sizes.
quotes: Achieving experimental quantum advantage would require, as a minimum, a QNN with width greater than 60 qubits, such that the dimensionality of the accessible feature space becomes classically intractable.
considerable research still remains into the scalabiltiy of our scheme, which was only demonstrated at the small sizes feasible on current quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion states the limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that how to fairly compare quantum and classical neural networks remains a significant open question, and that a simulator gain does not necessarily carry to current devices.
quotes: how to fairly compare quantum and classical neural networks still remains a significant open question.
it does not follow that such an improvement can necessarily be realised on current quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state both limits.
